# About

## Row 1 {height = 62.5%}

::: {.card title="Purpose"}
- This is a demo version of the H2Seq NSW HIV pipeline. 

- The dashboard rendered herein includes simulated notification data simulated atop 347 openly available sequences from [Di Giallonardo et al., 2021](https://doi.org/10.1002/jia2.25655). 

- [It is for demonstartion purposes only, and none of the vidualisations or results here have anything to do with reality.]{.mark}
:::

::: {.card title="Protecting identity"}
The developers of this report acknowledge that projecting molecular epidemiological results to the level
of the individual can potentially result in devastating outcomes for PLWH due to criminalisation and stigma. We further
believe that trust between the community, public health authorities, and clinical prividers is fundamental to this
report being mutually beneficial. To this end, the report was designed under the following constraints, which reflect UNAIDS guidelines on proper use of molecular epidemiology for HIV [@unaids_2025].

- All data incorporated in this report is de-identified via cryptographic hashing of initals and DOB information [@langevin_2026_distributed].
- All clustering methods are non-directional. That is, there is no phylogenetics used in this report to implicate directionality between clustered individuals.
- Diagrams do not explicitly link individuals, nor is the evolutionary distance between individual samples ever shown. [Therefore, for any cluster diagram, one cannot reasonably point to individual transmission events. This step is taken in acknowledgment of the fact that while non-directional clustering does not imply person-to-person transmission, it can still be used alongside circumstantial evidence to implicate individuals.]{.mark}
:::

## Row 2 {height = 37.5%}

### {.tabset}

::: {.card title="Sections"}
This report is structured into 5 sections:

- **Topline** — Key numbers for `r config$report$cutoff_lower` to `r config$report$cutoff_upper`.

- **Drug resistance** — Rates of resistance to drug classes, drugs, and surveillance drug resistance mutations (SDRMs).

- **Cluster trends** — Cluster size over time, which can be broken down for overseas/local acquisition and exposure categories.

- **Cluster explorer** — Visualises metadata for selections of clusters.

- **Supplementary** — Supplementary results, details of data preparation and analysis.
:::


::: {.card title="Key terms"}
| Abbreviation | Definition |
|--|---------|
| PLWH | People/person living with HIV |
| Cluster | 2 or more sequences from PLWH that fall below a specified genetic distance threshold |
| Active cluster | A cluster where at least one sample originates in the current reporting period |
| Singleton | An unclustered sequence |
| Pair | Two sequences forming a cluster of size 2 |
| Small cluster | A cluster of 3–9 individuals |
| Large cluster | A cluster of 10 or more individuals |
| SDRM | Surveillance drug resistance mutation |
| *pol* | HIV polymerase gene, with _prrt_ and _in_ regions |

:::

::: {.card title="Brief methods"}

| Step | Tool | Details |
|------|------|---------|
| Data preparation | Custom pipeline, [cawlign](https://github.com/veg/cawlign) | Sequences & notifications checked, linked to notifications, aligned to _pol_, and filtered |
| Drug resistance | [sierrapy](https://hivdb.stanford.edu/dr-summary/comments/PI/) | Stanford HIVdb algorithm for resistance interpretation and SDRM annotation |
| Clustering | [HIV-TRACE](https://github.com/veg/hivtrace) | TN93 pairwise distance clustering at `r config$hivtrace$threshold` subs/site |

See the Supplementary tab for more details.
:::
